cases.question: Does keyword cleanup expose conflicting duplicate metadata and apply the saved decision?
Do line-based keyword and crawl inputs keep their first entry even when a previous table setting marked the first row as a header?
Does crawl preparation enforce host, protocol, include, and exclude rules while preserving rejection reasons?
Does a pasted sitemap index stay separate from page crawl targets?
Does the robots evaluator select the longest applicable rule and Allow on an equal tie?
Does the crawl plan preserve the winning robots rule and every non-target group?
Does a recipe identify a moved column by name instead of silently reusing its old position?
Does the debugger treat a 200 response with noindex as technically blocked?
Does pasted response evidence produce the declared status, canonical, robots, and index signals?
Does a crawler export separate technical eligibility from noindex, robots, canonical, and conflicting signals?

observed.boundary: Technically eligible does not mean indexed, selected as canonical, ranking, or receiving traffic.

cases.question: Does the MCP lab identify and repair core tools/call structure?
Does the MCP session analyzer pair messages and expose unanswered and orphaned IDs?
Does a run manifest bind input, settings, and output without embedding source or export contents?

limits: These downloadable deterministic fixtures exercise parsing and decision logic. They do not crawl a live URL, query a search engine, or contact an MCP server.
The keyword fixture proves that conflicting metadata becomes visible and requires an explicit resolution; the receiving importer still requires a user-reviewed column mapping.
The MCP checks cover selected version-specific core fields and expected-shape comparison, not the complete normative schema or a real client/server exchange.
Robots, canonical, and indexability results remain bounded to the values supplied to the local functions.
